entities.summary:
Eleazar of Worms (unknown–1238) was a prominent Kabbalist and halakhic authority, among the greatest of the Hasidei Ashkenaz and a disciple of Rabbi Judah the Pious.

As a leading figure in 13th-century Jewish mysticism, Eleazar of Worms played a crucial role in the transmission of Kabbalistic knowledge from the Ashkenaz region to Eastern Europe. His treatise, the Book of the Perfumer, revealed the numerical value of 'Perfumer' to be equal to Eleazar, solidifying his reputation as a sage and mystic.

The impact of Eleazar's teachings can be seen in the works of later Kabbalists, such as Isaac Luria, who built upon Eleazar's ideas to develop the Kabbalistic tradition.

Eleazar's significance extends beyond his own time, as his writings demonstrate a deep understanding of Jewish law, mysticism, and the role of the human in the divine plan.

The influence of Eleazar's teachings can be seen in the proliferation of Kabbalistic texts and the establishment of Jewish mysticism as a distinct field of study.

Eleazar of Worms' legacy is a testament to the enduring power of Jewish mysticism and the importance of preserving and transmitting knowledge across generations.

In the words of Eleazar himself, 'The secrets of the universe are hidden in the numbers' (Book of the Perfumer).
